transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-05-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Dana Liu (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Hightower Head of Security), Evan Moore (Platform), Priya Nair (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on security controls and retention behavior observed in pilot. Reviewed initial audit log exports, SSO provisioning status, encryption/KMS questions, and a perf follow-up for Dedicated nodes. Agreed on artifacts to share and a perf run.

Topics:
- SSO (SAML + SCIM provisioning) status and open issues
- Audit log sampling, format, and forwarding to Splunk
- Data retention options (30/90/365) and legal holds
- SOC2 evidence and encryption/KMS details
- Small performance tune: batching/kv cache length and Dedicated kernel run

Action items (recap in meeting): see action_items field above

Transcript body:
00:00 Samir: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
00:05 Laura: Laura here, hi.
00:06 Evan: Evan, hi.
00:07 Priya: Priya on my side.
00:08 Dana: Dana from Redwood, hi all. Samir: cool, let's dive. We have about 55 minutes.
00:22 Samir: First item — SSO. Laura you mentioned earlier SCIM mapping was a little off. Where are we?
00:30 Laura: Yeah, our IdP team saw that some of the groups weren't mapping to the new roles, like the platform-admin group kept coming in as generic user. We traced it to the SAML assertion attribute name mismatch.
00:45 Dana: Right, on our side the mapping key expects "roles" or "groups" depending on the IdP. We do have a SCIM endpoint for provisioning, which will create the accounts and apply RBAC, but the initial SAML flow uses just attributes.
00:58 Evan: We tried SCIM but our provisioning flow is through Okta's group push, and it seems Redwood accepted the users but didn't attach the custom permissions.
01:12 Dana: That sounds like a mapping configuration. I'll share our example SCIM schema and the SAML attribute mapping in the notes. Also, note there's an edge case when SCIM creates service accounts vs human accounts, those need explicit role tags.
01:30 Laura: Ok, please send that. We need to show auditors the mapping during the SOC 2 walkthrough.
01:40 Samir: Speaking of SOC 2, I've got the Type II report. I'll scrub PII and send the control matrix and evidence guide after the call.
01:50 Priya: Great, that'll help. On retention: we've been testing 30-day retention in the pilot cluster and noticed some audit logs missing on day 28. Not sure if that's a query issue or retention truncation.
02:05 Dana: Hmm, ok can you give me the sample log IDs? Our console has a retention toggle per deployment in Redwood Console — though in the Private deployment that setting is surfaced to the customer admin. Could be a sampling vs full export problem.
02:20 Evan: We exported the logs to Splunk using the HTTP forwarder. The Splunk index shows gaps.
02:30 Dana: Are you using the out-of-band exporter or the streaming API? We have two modes — one that writes to S3-like storage for long-term, and a streaming forwarder. If the streaming forwarder saw retries it might be dropping events if the buffer overflowed.
02:50 Evan: We did an out-of-band S3 export for the main archive and streaming for real-time. The S3 archive appears complete but the Splunk streaming view has gaps.
03:05 Dana: Likely a client-side backpressure issue. I'll share the Splunk forwarder best practices. Also double-check the HTTP 5xx logs on our side, we'll correlate.
03:20 Laura: We also want immutability for certain audit records for compliance. How does Redwood lock logs?
03:30 Dana: For Hosted we can configure write-once S3 policies and lifecycle rules. In Dedicated/Private, you control the object store and can apply immutability (WORM) via your storage layer or KMS policies. Our audit events include a signed digest so you can detect tampering.
03:45 Priya: Are digests accessible for auditor review?
03:50 Samir: Yes, we can provide signed digests and a proof-of-origin log. I'll package an example with the SOC2 artifacts.
04:03 Evan: On encryption — we want to bring our own keys (BYOK) and HSM. Is that available?
04:12 Dana: Yes for Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS integration; HSM-backed keys for on-prem packages. For Hosted, BYOK is supported for vaulting but full HSM-managed keys depend on plan. There's a FIPS/HSM add-on for Dedicated enterprise customers.
04:35 Laura: Any latency impact when using customer KMS? We run low-latency inference and don't want a crypto hop on every request.
04:45 Dana: Good point. Keys are used for envelope encryption; per-request crypto is minimized. We keep session keys cached inside the runtime; KMS is called mainly for key wrapping/unwrapping during rotation. Practically negligible latency for token generation but we'll validate in the perf run.
05:05 Samir: That leads to the performance note — Evan you saw a 12% CPU bump under high-concurrency during the pilot?
05:15 Evan: Yes when we increased batch sizes to optimize cost we saw a CPU increase on the Dedicated GPU host and occasional token latency spikes around 99th percentile.
05:26 Dana: We suspect KV cache length and batching interplay. If KV cache is large and we do aggressive batching, kernel selection can move to a path that's less optimal on your host's driver version.
05:40 Evan: We're on a slightly older kernel in our Dedicated test rig. We can repro locally if Redwood can run a kernel-optimized job.
05:50 Dana: We'll schedule a kernel-level perf run on a Dedicated node with your workload. I'll coordinate with Samir and Evan after the call.
06:05 Laura: Back to compliance — we need SSO session revocation for offboarding. If someone is deprovisioned in Okta, are sessions killed immediately?
06:20 Dana: SCIM deprovisioning flows can trigger immediate revocation; SAML sessions have TTL. For Hosted flows we offer a webhook to push revocations. For Private, you can enforce central session management. We'll share our recommended offboarding playbook.
06:38 Priya: Also audit logs for key admin actions — who rotated keys, who changed RBAC. Are those surfaced?
06:48 Dana: Yes, there's an admin audit stream and an operator audit stream. Admin actions (RBAC changes, key rotations) are timestamped, include actor, and signed. We can increase retention for just that stream if you need longer than general request logs.
07:05 Samir: One more regulatory note — Hightower has EU residency requirements for a subset of customers. Are there region locks for data residency?
07:16 Dana: Yes, in Private deployments you can pin model storage and logs to regions. For Hosted we offer EU-only deployments and guaranteed routing, and you can route by policy so EU traffic stays in EU hosts. We'll need your list of datasets to classify.
07:30 Laura: We'll send the dataset classification to Priya and copy Redwood.
07:35 Evan: Quick question — what's the format of the audit log? JSON lines? CSV?
07:40 Dana: JSON lines, with a schema we published. Some fields are nested, and occasionally our exporter flattens nested arrays which confuses Splunk. I'll send the exact schema (and a pre-made Splunk sourcetype).
07:58 Laura: Great. Also want to verify retention tiers: 30 days for request logs, 90 for admin logs, 365 for archived incidents. Can Redwood enforce per-stream retention?
08:12 Dana: Yes per-stream retention is supported. We'll show you config in Console. For Private, it's enforced through your object store lifecycle rules.
08:25 Priya: Any support for legal hold so we don't expire data flagged by eDiscovery?
08:32 Samir: Yes, we have a hold API that marks objects to skip lifecycle expiration. We'll give the API spec.
08:40 Evan: On the Splunk export, what about ordering guarantees? We saw out-of-order events when bursting.
08:46 Dana: The streaming pipeline is best-effort; for strict ordering you should rely on the S3 archive which preserves append order. Real-time streams may be reordered during retries. We'll document sequence numbers in the event schema.
09:05 Laura: Ok, let's go through the short results we saw this week: 95th pct latency within SLA, 99th spiky under heavy batching, retention gaps in streaming, SCIM mapping partially fixed.
09:22 Dana: Correct. We also saw 0.02% token-level anomaly in one log subset — likely a parsing edge case. We'll supply a repro.
09:32 Samir: Next step recap — I'll share SOC2 and signed digest example, Dana will share Splunk forwarder guide and SCIM/SAML mapping templates, Evan will run retention toggles and perf, Priya will confirm retention/regulatory lists.
09:50 Priya: Can we get the artifacts before our internal audit next week?
09:55 Samir: We'll prioritize SOC2 artifacts and mapping docs — target 2027-05-14 delivery.
10:02 Dana: Scheduling note: I'll propose two windows for the Dedicated kernel run, target week of 2027-05-18.
10:12 Laura: Perfect. Anything else?
10:15 Evan: Not from platform.
10:16 Samir: Cool, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the thread with the docs.
10:22 Meeting end.
